Highly Regioselective Synthesis of Allene-Containing 2-
Benzoxepines

Introduction
As representative seven-membered oxygen-containing hetero-
cycles, 2-benzoxepines represent a significant structural motif in
numerous natural products and synthetic pharmaceuticals that
exhibit a wide range of biological and physiological activities
(Figure 1).<sup>[1]</sup> For example, Doxepin demonstrates both antide-
pressant and sedative-hypnotic effects,<sup>[2]</sup> Obtuanhydride
displays antifungal activity,<sup>[3]</sup> whereas xylarinols A has proven to
inhibit the activity of yeast α-glucosidase.<sup>[4]</sup> In view of the
importance of 2-benzoxepines, the establishment of efficient
and straightforward construction methods for synthesizing
these scaffolds has attracted considerable attention from the
organic synthesis community.<sup>[5]</sup>
In the past decades, tremendous advances have been
achieved in synthetic methods for the construction of 2-
benzoxepine skeletons, such as transannular macrocyclization
via intramolecular B-alkyl Suzuki reaction,<sup>[6]</sup> tandem

tion/Michael addition<sup>[7]</sup> and transition-metal-catalyzed [2 + 2 +
2] cyclotrimerization,<sup>[8]</sup> coupling annulation,<sup>[9]</sup> [5 + 2]
cycloaddition.<sup>[10]</sup> Nevertheless, the synthesis of seven-mem-
bered heterocycles continues to encounter significant chal-
lenges, primarily due to the unique thermodynamic and kinetic
properties of seven-membered nitrogen/oxygen-containing
heterocyclic skeletons, along with their own specific trans-
annular interactions.<sup>[11]</sup> Consequently, the development of novel
and efficient synthetic strategies to access 2-benzoxepine
skeletons is highly desirable.

the sequential formation of C� C and C� O bonds results in the

Intermolecular cycloadditions of allenes derivatives via
palladium-catalyzed have been discovered to efficiently inte-
grate various structural fragments while maintaining high atom
and step economy. Consequently, this method offers straight-
forward and effective approaches for the synthesis of
heterocycles.<sup>[12]</sup> Remarkably, Ma et al. employed the aforemen-
tioned strategy to develop a series of novel methods for
synthesizing complex six-membered oxygen-containing<sup>[13]</sup> and
eight-membered nitrogen-containing<sup>[14]</sup> heterocycles, utilizing
allene derivatives and propargylic carbonates as starting
materials. However, the synthesis of seven-membered hetero
cycles has not been reported to date. Inspired by these findings,
we envisioned a strategy for the construction of 2-benzoxepine
skeletons through decarboxylation/cycloaddition of propargylic
carbonates with benzyl allenyl ethers. Herein, we present our
efforts on Pd(0)-catalyzed intermolecular [5 + 2] cycloaddition,
which provides an ideal and concise approach for synthesizing
functionalized 2-benzoxepine frameworks Scheme 1.

With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we ex-
plored the scope and generality of the cyclization reaction
through a systematic investigation of the electronic nature of
the substituents on substrates 2 under the optimal conditions
(Table 2). The yield of the para-methoxy-substituted product 3 b
was 62 %, which was slightly lower than that of product 3a.
Additionally, the yield of the meta-methoxy-substituted ana-
logue 3 c further decreased to 55%. As the number of methoxy
substituent groups on the benzene ring of substrates 2
increased, the yields of the corresponding multi-methoxy-
substituted products 3 d and 3 e exhibited a downward trend.
The substrate 2 containing dioxygen substituent demonstrated
tolerance and afforded the desired cyclization product 3 f in
54 % yield. Notably, the naphthylmethyl allenyl ether was
successfully converted into 3 g, achieving a yield of 72 %, which
surpassed that of 3 a. The increase in yield may be attributed to
the electron effects of the naphthalene ring. Next, we
investigated the reactivity of benzyl allenyl ethers with fluorine
or chlorine substituents, successfully obtaining the target
products 3 h and 3 i in 43% and 55% yields, respectively.
However, the iodine-substituted substrate 2j did not give the
target product, which could be primarily attributed to the
oxidative insertion of Pd into the C�I bond, leading to an
unintended coupling reaction.<sup>[15]</sup> To our surprise, substrates 2
containing a strong EWG (CN,

products 3 k and 3 l in satisfactory yields. In summary, substrates
2 bearing EDG or EWG are well tolerated, delivering corre-
sponding products in moderate to good yields.
To further evaluate the robustness of the methodology, the
reactivity of dioxygen-substituted propargylic carbonate 1 b
and diverse benzyl allenyl ethers 2 was investigated (Table 3).
The catalytic system similarly demonstrated tolerance to the
reaction of 1 b with benzyl allenyl ethers 2 which were
substituted with methoxyl, fluorine, chlorine, trifluoromethyl
and cyano groups, as well as with naphthylmethyl allenyl ether,
yielding 2-benzoxepines in 35% to 60% (4a–4h). A comparison
of the yields of 3a and 4a, 3b and
{ \mathfrak { 4 } } \mathbf { b } ,
3d and 4c, 3g and 4d,
3 h and 4e, 3 i and 4 f, 3 k and 4 g, as well as 3 l and 4 h revealed
that, when reacting with the same benzyl allenyl ether 2, the
yields of 2-benzoxepines synthesized from substrate 1 b were
lower than those synthesized from substrate 1 a. This observa-
tion indicated that the presence of electron-withdrawing
substituents on the benzene ring of substrates 1 was not
favorable for the reaction. As anticipated, benzyl allenyl ethers
with a methyl substituent at the ortho or para position of the
allenyl ether group underwent transformations smoothly,
generating the corresponding products in 57 % and 58% yields,
respectively (4 i and 4j). However, due to steric hindrance, the
yield of the isopropyl-substituted product 4 k was limited to
only 44%.
Following the above experiments, we devoted our attention
to various leaving groups on propargylic carbonates (Table 4).
The reactions involving propargyl ethyl carbonate 1 c and
propargyl benzyl carbonate 1d demonstrated good compati-
bility and yielded acceptable results under the tested conditions
(entries 1 and 2). In contrast, propargyl phosphate 1 e exhibited
lower reactivity, potentially due to the reduced leaving ability
of phosphate compared to that of the aforementioned
carbonates (entry 3).

Conclusions
In summary, we have discovered a hitherto undescribed
method for the synthesis of allene-containing 2-benzoxepines
via palladium-catalyzed intermolecular [5 + 2] cycloaddition.
Notably, this novel protocol features easy substrates availability,
broad substrates scope, decent yields and excellent regioselec-

Conclusions
In summary, we have discovered a hitherto undescribed
method for the synthesis of allene-containing 2-benzoxepines
via palladium-catalyzed intermolecular [5 + 2] cycloaddition.
